title: What is the static keyword and where can it be used?
shortTitle: What is the static keyword and why is main static?
keyPoints: static means "belongs to the class, not to any object" – one shared copy for all instances
static field: one copy shared by all objects (e.g., a bank-wide interest rate or a counter)
static method: called on the class, not on an object – cannot access instance fields or this
static block: runs once when the class is loaded, used for one-time initialization
static nested class: a nested class that does not need an instance of the outer class
main is static because the JVM calls it before any object exists

s1_definition.oneliner: static means the member belongs to the class itself, not to any particular object. There is one shared copy, accessed via the class name.
s1_definition.profdef:
static can be applied to four things:

- **static field:** One copy shared by all instances. Stored in Metaspace with the class, not on the heap with each object.
- **static method:** Called on the class (`Account.getCount()`) without creating an object. Cannot use `this` or access instance fields.
- **static initializer block:** Code that runs once when the class is first loaded. Used for complex one-time setup.
- **static nested class:** A class defined inside another class that does not require an outer instance.
s1_definition.analogy: A bank's base interest rate is static: there is one rate for the whole bank, not a separate copy per customer. Any branch can read it via the head office (class name), and changing it affects everyone. A customer's balance is instance: each customer has their own copy.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  static = belongs to the CLASS, not to any object

  static field:    one copy, shared by all instances, in Metaspace
  static method:   called on the class, no 'this', no instance fields
  static block:    runs once when class is loaded
  static nested:   inner class that needs no outer instance

  Access rules:
    static  → can access static only
    instance → can access both static and instance

  Why main is static:
    JVM starts → no objects exist → needs static entry point
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The static keyword means "belongs to the class, not to any object." A static field has one shared copy for all instances. A static method is called on the class without creating an object. A static initializer block runs once when the class is loaded. And a static nested class does not need an instance of its enclosing class.

The main method is static because the JVM must call it before any object exists. Static methods cannot access `this` or instance fields – they can only work with other static members or with objects passed to them as parameters.

In banking, static is used for shared constants (base interest rate), counters (account count), utility methods (interest calculation), and configuration initialization. But mutable static fields shared across threads need synchronization.

One sentence to remember: static means one copy for the class, no object needed – static can access static, instance can access both, but static cannot access instance.
